title: The voice note
label: THEY HAVEN'T HEARD YOU THIS WEEK
lead: Hook 1, the object truth: the phone that hears you all day against parents who haven't, a contrast a stranger gets with no context.

hooks.label: THEY HAVEN'T HEARD YOU THIS WEEK
hooks.say: Your phone hears your voice all day. Your parents haven't heard it this week.

hooks.label: THE VOICE NOTE YOU DELETED
hooks.say: You hold the mic, say hi Mum, then cancel it before it sends.

hooks.label: WHEN DID THEY LAST HEAR YOU?
hooks.say: When did your parents last hear your actual voice, and not a text?

beats.say: Your phone hears your *voice* all day. Your parents haven't heard it this week.
beats.scene: A phone on a dark table buzzing, screen full of a live voice waveform, a pushed-in camera.

beats.say: Their chat is right there, a *microphone* you never hold.
beats.scene: Overhead on the phone: a chat titled Mum & Dad at the top, a round mic button pulsing, untouched.

beats.say: You keep saving it for *later*, for when there's news.
beats.scene: A night desk. A wall clock spins forward, books stack up, the phone face down beside a mug.

beats.say: But they don't need news, they just want to hear you're *okay*.
beats.scene: A different room: warm kitchen at home, two mugs and an old phone on a table, screen dark, waiting.

beats.say: So hold it down and say *hi*. That's the whole message.
beats.scene: Back on your phone: the mic button presses in, a waveform grows, the word hi drawn as the wave.

beats.say: Send this to someone whose parents are still waiting on that *voice* *note*.
beats.scene: The kitchen again: the old phone lights up with a play button, warm light swells across the room.
